methodologyNote: Twenty-five questions drawn from this tool's real domain (Irish and EU nonprofit funding, textile EPR and related EU regulation, corporate commitments, and reuse/social-value impact factors), roughly six per domain, mixing lookup, filter and synthesis. Ground truth was established by hand from a primary source first and recorded per question; each side was graded blind against it. Cala side: one call per question via knowledge_search (narrative/lookup/synthesis) or knowledge_query (F3, F7, which are list-shaped); no retries and no duplicate inputs, so a weak result is recorded as-is. Web side: one WebSearch call per question, answered from the returned results block only. tokensConsumed is the count the answering agent must read to produce a cited answer, measured with a single fixed tokeniser (js-tiktoken, cl100k_base) over: for Cala, the returned answer payload (the knowledge_search content field, or the knowledge_query results rows); for web, the WebSearch results block (titles, URLs and snippet/synthesis text) with the fixed reminder boilerplate excluded. Reproduce it by re-running each query and counting the same text with the committed script scripts/benchmark/count-tokens.mjs. citationReturned records whether the method returned at least one resolvable source URL. latencyMs is deliberately omitted: this harness does not expose reliable per-call timing and inventing figures would breach the no-fabrication rule. IMPORTANT FAIRNESS CAVEAT: the Cala figure is the slim answer payload. Cala's DEFAULT response also returns large explainability and context provenance arrays; measured in full, one sampled question (F1) came to 1881 tokens versus 331 for the answer alone (about 5.7x), larger than the web block for the same question. So Cala's token advantage exists only when the response is deliberately slimmed (content only, explainability=false, return_entities=false). Aggregate result across 25 questions: Cala answer payloads totalled 6389 tokens (avg ~256), web results blocks 11044 (avg ~442), so Cala was about 1.7x leaner on this measure, well short of the roughly 8x public claim, which would require a web baseline of reading full source pages rather than a modern search API's synthesised snippets. Correctness: Cala 25/25, web 24/25 (web missed the true maximum grant in F4). Citations: web 25/25; Cala 23/25, since knowledge_query (F3, F7) returned rows without sources. Cala credit cost of the run: 25 credits.

questions.question: Why should clothing reuse life cycle assessments not assume one-for-one substitution?

results.answerSummary: Empirical substitution ~45-68%, impulse/additive buying, the secondhand paradox, and 64% of LCAs assume 1:1 without basis; still beneficial but the credit is overstated.
